questions.q: What is the definition of 'exposition' in the context of a one-act play? Provide an example from the opening of "जटुह".
questions.a: Exposition is the part of the plot that introduces the setting, characters, and initial conflict. In "जटुह", the exposition occurs in the opening dialogue between जटुह and वफर् where we learn about वफर्'s tuition, his father's absence, and the pressure of exams. A wrong answer would confuse exposition with the inciting incident (e.g., saying the mother's entry is the exposition), showing the student cannot distinguish the initial setup from the event that complicates the plot.

questions.q: Explain in your own words how the playwright uses 'French scenes' (character entrances/exits) to structure the rising action in "जटुह".
questions.a: The playwright structures rising action through a series of French scenes: each time a new character enters (यथक, ग्स्मेकल्वज, इफर, लैक्नद, etc.), the conflict escalates from a private tuition dispute to a systemic critique of education. A wrong answer might list entrances but not explain how each escalates the conflict, indicating the student sees structure as a list rather than a causal chain.

questions.q: Apply the concept of 'climax' to the play: Identify the climax of "जटुह" and justify your choice using a specific dialogue or stage direction.
questions.a: The climax occurs when जटुह confronts the principal (ग्स्मेकल्वज) and refuses to back down, declaring she will file a complaint against the coaching mafia (around page 81-82). This is the turning point because the conflict shifts from personal to institutional. A wrong answer might pick the emotional reunion of वफर् and his mother, which is part of the falling action, showing the student cannot distinguish the peak of tension from its release.

questions.q: Analyze how the single-act structure (no interval, continuous time) contributes to the play's theme of relentless academic pressure.
questions.a: The continuous single-act structure traps the audience in the same unbroken timeline as the characters, mirroring the student's inability to escape the cycle of tuition, exams, and parental expectations. There is no intermission to 'breathe', just as वफर् gets no respite. A wrong answer would focus only on convenience of staging, missing the thematic resonance of structural choice.

questions.q: Evaluate the effectiveness of the play's resolution: Does the ending (जटुह deciding to launch a movement) provide a satisfying closure to the central conflict? Argue with evidence.
questions.a: The resolution is intentionally open-ended: जटुह's decision to start a movement (page 83) suggests the systemic issue persists, which is realistic but not a neat closure. This effectiveness lies in its refusal to offer a false solution, aligning with the play's critical tone. A wrong answer might demand a happy ending (e.g., वफर् gets relief), revealing an expectation of conventional resolution over thematic integrity.

questions.q: Create an alternative ending for "जटुह" that changes the narrative structure from linear to circular (ending where it began). Write a brief scenario (3-4 sentences) showing how this would alter the play's message.
questions.a: A circular ending could show जटुह back in her tuition room with a new student, repeating the same dialogue about homework, implying the system is unchangeable. This would shift the message from potential activism to hopeless cyclical traps. A poor answer would simply rewrite the ending without explaining the structural change's thematic impact, showing the student doesn't grasp how structure shapes meaning.
